subject: gk
question: Milk is good source of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium, phosphorous, and protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Calcium** is essential for the development and maintenance of strong bones and teeth. It also plays a vital role in muscle function, nerve transmission, and hormonal secretion.
 
• **Phosphorous** works closely with calcium to build strong bones and teeth. It is also involved in the body's energy production and storage processes.
 
• **Protein** is crucial for the repair and growth of tissues, production of enzymes and hormones, and maintenance of a healthy immune system.
 
• Milk is widely regarded as one of the most complete foods due to its rich content of essential nutrients including vitamins and minerals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium**

 
 
• Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body, accounting for about 1-2% of an adult's body weight.
 
• It is vital for the formation and maintenance of bones and teeth. About 99% of the body's calcium is stored in the bones and teeth, providing structure and strength.
 
• Calcium also plays a key role in blood clotting, muscle contraction, and the functioning of the heart and nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorous**
 
 
• Phosphorous is the second most abundant mineral in the body. About 85% of the body's phosphorus is found in bones and teeth.
 
• It is essential for the formation of bones and teeth, energy production, and storage, and it helps in the formation of DNA and RNA.
 
• Phosphorous also aids in the utilization of carbohydrates and fats and the synthesis of protein for the growth, maintenance, and repair of cells and tissues.
 
 
 
• **Protein**
 
 
• Proteins are large, complex molecules that play many critical roles in the body. They are made up of hundreds or thousands of smaller units called amino acids.
 
• Proteins are essential for the structure, function, and regulation of the body's tissues and organs.
 
• They are involved in various bodily functions, including catalyzing metabolic reactions, DNA replication, responding to stimuli, and transporting molecules from one location to another.
